pages-router.text: A page or an API route of the Pages Router. The plugin runs the routes of `app/`.

prerendered-pages.text: A page that a build prerenders, like one with `generateStaticParams`. Next keeps it between two requests, and here every request renders its page.

one-request-at-a-time.text: A navigation while a Server Action is in flight. The server handles one request at a time.

another-origin.text: A redirect or a navigation to another origin. The tab cannot leave the test.

javascript-off.text: Opens the page with JavaScript off. The test runs in the tab of the page.

build-output.text: Reads the output of `next build`: a manifest, a chunk or a prerendered file in `.next`.

cli-output.text: Reads what the Next.js CLI prints: the table of routes of a build, a warning when it starts, or what Tailwind logs as the build compiles the CSS.

playwright-page.text: Uses Playwright's `Page` itself: `page.route()` to stand in for a response, or an event of a frame.

page-load-requests.text: Counts the requests of a page load, a form post or a redirect. The shim sees what the page fetches, not what the plugin fetches to load a page.

node-in-test.text: The test itself needs Node.js: it starts a server, or removes a directory.
node-in-test.match: the test runs in a tab, not in Node\.js|it starts a process, opens a socket or reads a build|__dirname is not defined

shared-history.text: Expects the `history.length` of a new tab. The tests of a file share the history of the tab, which ends at 50 entries.

state-between-tests.text: Expects the cookie that an earlier test of the file set. The plugin's `cleanup()` clears the cookies after every test.

changes-the-app.text: Changes a file of the app, or builds or starts the app itself.
changes-the-app.match: needs a new build, or a dev server|runs the Next\.js CLI itself|changes the app before it is built

dynamic-css-manifest.text: The CSS of a component of `next/dynamic`, which Next links from its manifest of dynamic imports, with `precedence="dynamic"`, next to a preload of its JavaScript. Here it is a stylesheet of the segment that imports the component.

css-not-minified.text: Expects the CSS that Next's build minified. The run serves the CSS that Vite compiles, as it is.

css-chunks.text: Counts the stylesheets of a page. Next's build puts the CSS files that a segment imports in one chunk. The run serves the CSS of the dev server, where each file is a stylesheet of its own.

og-image-response.text: An image that `ImageResponse` of `next/og` renders. Next renders it with WebAssembly and a font of its own, which it reads from its own files with `node:fs`, and the server's disk here has no file of the project.

streamed-to-prerendered.text: Expects the HTML of a page that Next's build prerenders. Here the page renders for the request, as `next start` renders a dynamic page: React sends the `<link rel="preconnect">` of a font in the `Link` header, and a client navigation commits before the metadata that Next streams after the page.

router-act.text: Uses `createRouterAct()` of Next's test library, which holds back the requests of the router and answers them with Playwright's `page.route()`.

another-app.text: Asks for another app than the fixture: files of its own, or another `next.config`. The runner runs one app for a fixture, the fixture as it is or as `fixtures.ts` prepares it.
another-app.match: builds the app out of files the test names|changes the app before it is built

next-development-checks.text: Expects the production code of Next, which leaves out the checks of its development code, like the error for a `<Link>` with a dynamic `href`. The plugin runs Next's development code by default, as its `build` option says.

dynamic-params.text: A path that `generateStaticParams` does not list, of a route with `dynamicParams = false`. Next answers 404 for it from the paths its build prerendered. Here no build lists them, and the page renders.

not-a-page.text: A navigation of Next's router to a route handler that answers with JSON, which a browser shows in place of the app. The tab cannot leave the test, so the page stays, with an uncaught error.

config-set-cookies.text: Two `Set-Cookie` headers of one rule of `headers()` in `next.config` arrive as one. Next's build hands an adapter the headers of a rule as an object, which keeps one value per name, and `@next/routing` sets them from that.

legacy-react-dom-server.text: A Client Component that renders markup with `renderToStaticMarkup()` of `react-dom/server`. The ssr layer has Next's aliases of its edge runtime, where `react-dom/server` has React's renderer for web streams alone. A route on Node.js gets React's whole entry.

proxy-after.text: An `after()` of the proxy. What the proxy hands to `waitUntil()` runs after the proxy has returned, without its request stores, and Next needs them to run the callbacks.

exited-action-store.text: A promise of a Server Action, passed to `after()`, that calls a request API once the action is done. Next renders the page after the action outside the store of the action, with `AsyncLocalStorage.exit()`. Here the store stays exited for the rest of the request, so Next takes the call for one of the page.

commonjs-source.text: A source file of the app with `require` or `module.exports`. Vite serves the source files of the app as ES modules.

opens-a-response.text: Opens the response of a route handler that a browser shows as it is, like plain text or JSON. The plugin opens the pages of the app, and the test stays where it is.
opens-a-response.match: which is not a page to open

env-of-the-config.text: Passes `env` to `nextTestSetup()` for `next.config` to read. The runner loads the config once, before the first test, so every `describe` gets the same app.

server-error-log.text: Expects only the log of a Server Component's error as `next start` prints it: after a `⨯`, without the frames of Next. The server logs it to the tab's console, with the stack of the browser, and the client's own log of the error is in the same console.
